I'm building with native-dates, a date library on the browser's Temporal and Intl APIs. Read this docs page: {url}

Summarize what it teaches in one short paragraph and a few bullets, assuming I haven't read it. Then ask me what I'm building and what I want to learn, and answer from the documentation.

home.description: Natural-language dates built on the browser’s Temporal and Intl APIs. Chainable, immutable, and timezone-aware with zero dependencies.
home.hero.title: Your browser’s native dates in plain English
home.hero.lede: Temporal and Intl gave the browser real time zones, DST-safe calendar math, and locale formatting. Native Dates wraps them in a readable, immutable API in {size} br.
home.prims.title: Native primitives for every measure of time
home.prims.lede: Instead of working around the limitations of JS Date to store time zones or durations, use standards-enforced purpose-built time formats idiomatically.
home.consoles.title: Date gets them wrong. Temporal gets them right.
home.consoles.lede: Don’t spend time learning all of Date’s bugs and edge cases like it’s still 1995.
home.consoles.day.ask: What day is 2026-09-01 in New York?
home.consoles.day.why: Date parses ISO date strings as UTC midnight, which is 8 PM the previous evening in New York. CalendarDate has no time zone offset to shift.
home.consoles.month.ask: What is one month after January 31?
home.consoles.month.why: Date overflows February 31 into March 3. Temporal clamps to the end of February.
home.consoles.clocks.ask: What time is one day after 9 AM on March 7 in New York?
home.consoles.clocks.why: DST springs forward that night, making the day 23 hours long. Adding 24 hours shifts the clock to 10 AM. Temporal adds one calendar day and keeps 9 AM.
home.consoles.start.ask: Add 30 days to start to get due. What is start now?
home.consoles.start.why: setDate() mutates the Date instance in place. native-dates values are immutable, so plus() returns a new instance.
home.year.title: Avoid learning the entire world’s confusing relationship with time
home.year.lede: Los Angeles and Berlin switch DST on different weekends, changing their offset {changes} a year. Temporal’s IANA database gives you that for free with zero bytes shipped in your bundle.
home.year.caption: A 9:30 AM Los Angeles standup converted to Berlin time across {year}. For {days}, the offset narrows from {far} hours to {near}, shifting the meeting to {time}.
home.xray.title: Temporal’s precision, without the boilerplate
home.xray.lede: Temporal is explicit and low-level by design. Compare the same four operations in native-dates, raw Temporal, and JS Date.

home.try.lede: Switch the preview’s time zone to simulate running in another city, or edit the code live.
home.try.label: Live example: a meeting across zones
home.bytes.title: The whole core is {size}
home.bytes.lede: Core includes dates, times, zoned datetimes, durations, partial dates, ranges, calendar math, time zones, and formatting with zero dependencies. Toggle opt-in plugins to measure the combined bundle.

plugins.preset.compat.description: Relative time, lenient parsing, and legacy `Date` getters for migrating from Moment or Day.js.

plugins.loose.description: Lenient fallback parsing for human-written strings like `'March 5, 2026'`, returning `null` when unparseable.
